subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: What lifecycle contract should stable and generated hook session keys use: backward-compatible retained isolation, explicit ephemeral disposal, or persistent multi-turn reuse, and under which modes may transcripts be deleted?
rationale: Current main always creates a fresh isolated run but persists its row, while the cleanup request and the open persistent-reuse request require incompatible outcomes unless explicit modes and defaults are selected.

options.title: Explicit hook session modes
options.body: Keep current behavior as the compatibility default and add explicit ephemeral and persistent modes with mode-specific cleanup and transcript rules.

options.title: Retention-only policy
options.body: Add only a hook TTL and leave completion disposal and stable-key persistence for later work.

options.title: Shared ephemeral primitive
options.body: Design a generic core ephemeral-session contract first, then expose hooks as one caller alongside cron and other task-scoped runs.

recommendation.title: Explicit hook session modes
recommendation.body: Keep current behavior as the compatibility default and add explicit ephemeral and persistent modes with mode-specific cleanup and transcript rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior detailed review and broad hook/session history provide the strongest available product-routing signal for choosing user-facing defaults.
